title: Count the separate groups
prompt: The connections in graph are two-way. Return the number of separate groups: sets of names that can reach each other. A name with no connections is a group of its own. An empty graph has 0 groups.
hints: What does one breadth-first search from a name find?
It finds that name's whole group. So each search that starts from a name not yet seen is one new group.
Keep one seen Set for the whole function. For each name: if it is not seen, add 1 to the count and search from it, marking everything it reaches.
checkLabels: Every place can reach every other, so there is one group.
a and b, c alone, and d and e are three groups.
An empty graph has no groups.
One name alone is one group.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Marks only the direct neighbours of each start, not the whole group.
Assumes there is always at least one group.

feedback: One search marks one whole group. Count how many searches you have to start.
